title: Powers of 10 Worksheets: Multiplying and Dividing
intro: Teach powers of ten as changes in place value.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Use a chart to track each digit when multiplying or dividing by 10, 100, or 1,000. Name the value before and after.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

4.2 → 42 → 420 → 4,200

Each step multiplies the value by ten. Track the 4 from ones to tens, hundreds, and thousands.

Ask your student

How many times as large is this digit's value now?

If your student needs help

If the student adds or removes zeros indiscriminately, use a decimal example to check the shortcut.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each set contains one multiplication and one division question for each of 10, 100, and 1,000. Original starting values range from 0.1 through 99.9, including whole numbers. Selected answers have at most three decimal places.
